title: Model card metadata extension proposal - notes
content:
Purpose and high-level goal:

This is a working sketch for extending the existing lightweight model-card idea into a structured metadata payload that the Redwood runtime and calling clients can use to improve routing, fallbacks, cost estimates, and developer UX. The aim is not to replace full model cards or eval artifacts, but to add a concise, machine-readable set of fields surfaced via the models API (and optionally in the model catalog) that capture serving-relevant characteristics.

Design constraints / goals (working):
- concise: single payload < 8KB for common models
- backward compatible: falls back gracefully if fields missing
- actionable: contains hints both for client routing and server kernel/quant config
- privacy-safe: no training data PII; only aggregate descriptors
- variant-first: support multiple build/quantized/arch variants for a model

Primary consumers:
- Redwood router (cost/latency-based routing)
- Console / catalog UI
- Client SDKs for preflight checks and cost estimation
- SRE/ops teams for capacity planning

Proposed top-level fields (short bullets, expand in content):
- model_id: canonical id string (e.g. redwood/manticore-1)
- display_name: human readable
- family: small/medium/large or model family name
- architecture: decoder|encoder-decoder|encoder
- primary_use_cases: list (chat, code, embedding, rerank)
- input_max_tokens: integer (recommended safe max)
- typical_seq_dist: short histogram or enum (short|mixed|long)
- latency_profile: comma-separated SLO hints (p50,p95 at 8k tokens?)
- cost_profile: indicative cost units or tokens-per-dollar estimate
- quantization_variants: summary string listing available quant levels and expected perf impact
- kernels_supported: short list of runtime kernel hints (flash_attn_v2, triton_fused_gemm)
- memory_footprint_mb: rough GPU memory footprint for different sequence lengths (as small table string)
- recommended_batching: suggestion string like "prefill: batch=8,streaming: batch=1"
- legal_and_usage: high-level allowed content flags (PII_allowed:false, commercial_use:true, safety_notes: short)
- provenance: training-corpus-agg string, last_fine_tuned_date
- eval_summary: one-liner with link id to full eval set (Confluence id or eval job id)

Example minimal payload (pseudo-json as an API shape, clients should treat as opaque text blob if unknown fields appear):

{
  "model_id": "redwood/manticore-1",
  "display_name": "Manticore v1 (open)",
  "family": "manticore",
  "architecture": "decoder",
  "primary_use_cases": ["chat", "completion"],
  "input_max_tokens": 4096,
  "typical_seq_dist": "mixed",
  "latency_profile": "p50:12ms@8k,p95:45ms@8k",
  "cost_profile": "est_tokens_per_usd:25000",
  "quantization_variants": ["fp16", "8bit-quant"],
  "kernels_supported": ["flash_attn_v2", "fused_gelu"],
  "memory_footprint_mb": "8kseq:12000,2kseq:4000",
  "recommended_batching": "prefill:8,streaming:1",
  "legal_and_usage": {"commercial_use":true,"pii_allowed":false},
  "provenance": "web-crawl:curated-2019-2022",
  "eval_summary": "win rate vs baseline 0.87 (EVAL-2024-09)"
}

Notes on fields above:
- latency_profile: should be a tiny string so old clients can show an estimate without parsing heavy structures. Runtime will surface a richer numeric breakdown in admin APIs.
- quantization_variants: list the variants we ship; the runtime can map these to available Dedicated/Private images.
- kernels_supported: hints only — runtime chooses kernels based on target hardware + config.

API surface proposals (minimal additions):
1) GET /v1/models/:model_id/card?variant=8bit&hardware_hint=gpu
   - returns the model-card metadata payload for the resolved variant
   - query params: variant (optional), hardware_hint (optional: gpu/cpu/tpu)
   - headers: Accept: application/json; suggestions header: X-Redwood-Model-Hint

2) When listing models (GET /v1/models), include a compact card snippet (model_id, display_name, family, primary_use_cases, input_max_tokens) to make UI fast.

3) Optional streaming of large eval links: if eval_summary has external id, clients should request /v1/models/:id/card?detail=evals to fetch expanded eval metadata.

Runtime / serving integration ideas:
- Router uses typical_seq_dist + latency_profile + cost_profile to compute a routing score (latency-first routes to smaller family, cost-first to quantized variant).
- Autoscaler uses memory_footprint_mb table to decide which VM/GPU class to allocate for new variants.
- Kernel selection: if kernels_supported contains an entry not compatible with hardware, runtime will ignore but log a warning (no hard fail).

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How much legal detail do we store? (store flags only, link out for long legal text)
- Do we keep a histogram for seq lengths? storing a small encoded histogram (e.g., buckets "0-128,128-512,512-2k,2k+") might be useful.
- Compression: many model cards will include repeatable strings; should we canonicalize kernel names and quant names in a registry?
- Ownership & governance: who signs off on model_card content for public models vs internal fine-tunes?

Backward compatibility & migration plan:
- Start with optional fields: runtime treats missing fields as unknown and uses default heuristics.
- Publish a migration checklist for partners who onboard models to populate recommended fields (simple template).

Console / UX notes (quick ideas):
- In catalog list show a small badge for "latency tier" derived from latency_profile.
- In model detail page: show memory footprint slider so users can estimate Dedicated GPU class.
- In rollout UI: surface eval_summary warnings (if win rate vs baseline < 0.8, flag for QA).

Example small ASCII flow for how client uses the card when choosing a route:

User -> SDK chooses model_id + usage
SDK calls GET /models/:id/card?hardware_hint=gpu
SDK reads typical_seq_dist + recommended_batching -> decides prefer-variant=8bit
SDK estimates tokens-per-dollar from cost_profile -> shows estimate to developer
Router receives call -> runtime uses card latency_profile + kernel hints -> selects node pool and kernel

Actionable TODOs (short):
- [ ] Finalize canonical names for kernel strings and quant variants (small registry PR)
- [ ] Sample 10 model cards from open catalog and fill fields to test payload sizes
- [ ] Add minimal GET /models/:id/card implementation in dev environment
- [ ] Draft migration guide for partners + checklist doc on Confluence (link above)

Notes-of-record / quick references: 
- Related ticket: GH PR-422 (linked above) for adding variant metadata to model manifest
- Confluence stub: MC-1287 (evals linking standard)

Rough draft ends here — this is intended as a personal scratchpad to iterate with Mateo and Chen before turning into a short RFC.

Unresolveds I want feedback on from kernel/runtime owners:
- Is memory_footprint_mb represented as a tiny table string acceptable for autoscaler, or do you need a numeric matrix?
- How do we want to represent quantization degradation estimates? (percent latency/cost delta vs fp16?)

End of notes.
